baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, LTP 20260529 prebuilt: 9 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped. Per assertion, on a pty master fd from openpty(): (1) TCGETA on fd -1 -> EBADF(9); (2) TCGETS on fd -1 -> EBADF(9); (3) TCGETA with arg (struct termio*)-1 -> EFAULT(14); (4) TCGETS with arg (struct termios*)-1 -> EFAULT(14); (5) cmd 9999999 (0x98967f) -> ENOTTY(25); (6) TCGETA on a regular-file fd -> ENOTTY(25); (7) TCGETS on a regular-file fd -> ENOTTY(25); (8) TCGETA with arg NULL -> EFAULT(14); (9) TCGETS with arg NULL -> EFAULT(14). Direct host probe (/tmp/tcgeta/p.c, gcc -lutil) pins the specification behind those numbers: TCGETA(0x5405) succeeds with ret=0 on BOTH the pty master and the pty slave, and so do TCSETA(0x5406), TCSETAW(0x5407) and TCSETAF(0x5408) on the master; sizeof(struct termio)==18 and sizeof(struct termios)==60; the legacy termio returned by TCGETA is a pure truncation of termios -- its c_cc[0..8] is byte-identical to the termios c_cc[0..8] (03 1c 7f 15 04 00 01 00) and its four flag words are the termios u32 flags narrowed to u16 (iflag=0x500 oflag=0x5 cflag=0xbf lflag=0x8a3b), with c_line copied. So the correct kernel treats TCGETA as a first-class tty mode ioctl that differs from TCGETS only in the userspace struct layout, and an invalid arg pointer is therefore reached and reported as EFAULT.
failing_assertion: 2 of 9 fail, both TCGETA-on-a-tty cases, and both with the same wrong errno. qemu.log (KIRK_VERBOSE run): `ioctl01.c:62: TFAIL: Termio address is invalid expected EFAULT: ENOTTY (25)` (tcases[2]: fd=amaster, TCGETA, arg=(struct termio *)-1) and `ioctl01.c:62: TFAIL: Termio is NULL expected EFAULT: ENOTTY (25)` (tcases[7]: fd=amaster, TCGETA, arg=NULL). Asterinas returns ENOTTY(25) where Linux returns EFAULT(14). The 7 remaining cases pass, including both regular-file ENOTTY cases and all three TCGETS pointer cases, so the split is exactly along TCGETA vs TCGETS. Asterinas run summary: Passed 7, Failed 2, Broken 0.
root_cause: The legacy `struct termio` ioctl family is absent from the entire tree. `kernel/src/device/tty/ioctl_defs.rs` lines 8-19 define only the modern set -- TCGETS 0x5401, TCSETS 0x5402, TCSETSW 0x5403, TCSETSF 0x5404 over `OutData<CTermios>`/`InData<CTermios>`, the TCGETS2 0x542A family over `CTermios2`, and TIOCGWINSZ/TIOCSWINSZ. TCGETA 0x5405, TCSETA 0x5406, TCSETAW 0x5407 and TCSETAF 0x5408 have no `ioc!` alias; grep for `TCGETA`, `0x5405` and `CTermio\b` across kernel/ and ostd/ returns zero hits, and `kernel/src/device/tty/termio.rs` defines CTermios (line 315, four u32 flag words + u8 c_line + [u8; 19] c_cc) and CTermios2 (line 421) but no 18-byte legacy CTermio type at all. The mechanism that turns that omission into the wrong errno is the dispatch order. `sys_ioctl` (kernel/src/syscall/ioctl.rs:15-45) resolves the fd first -- which is why the two fd=-1 cases correctly yield EBADF before any cmd decoding -- then calls `file_owned.ioctl(raw_ioctl)`. For the pty master that reaches `PtyMaster::ioctl` (kernel/src/device/pty/master.rs:153-243), whose first arm is an explicit whitelist at lines 158-162 forwarding `GetTermios | GetTermios2 | SetTermios | SetTermios2 | SetTermiosWait | SetTermios2Wait | SetTermiosFlush | SetTermios2Flush | GetWinSize | SetWinSize | GetPtyNumber` to `self.slave.ioctl(raw_ioctl)`; TCGETA is not in that list, so it falls to the master's default arm at 236-243, which tries `terminal.job_ioctl(raw_ioctl, true)` and then bails with `return_errno_with_message!(Errno::ENOTTY, "the ioctl command is unknown")`. Even if it were forwarded, the shared `Tty::ioctl` (kernel/src/device/tty/mod.rs:225-338) has no TCGETA arm either and its own default arm at 320-334 ends in the same ENOTTY after trying job_ioctl and the driver hook. Because the cmd is rejected before any argument is touched, the code never performs the `cmd.write(&termio)` that would fault on the user pointer -- `Ioctl::write` -> `with_data_ptr_unchecked_access` -> `SafePtr::write` is what produces EFAULT for the TCGETS cases, and it is simply never reached. That is precisely why TCGETS with arg -1 and arg NULL both pass while the identical TCGETA cases both fail: the errno is decided by cmd recognition, not by pointer validity, and an unrecognised cmd masks the fault. Note the decoding machinery itself is fine -- 0x5405 is a valid legacy encoding (upper 16 bits zero, so `Ioctl::try_from_raw` at kernel/src/util/ioctl/mod.rs:219-251 takes the legacy branch and does not size-check the data), so nothing beyond a definition plus a handler arm is required.
invariant: A TTY must accept the legacy `struct termio` mode ioctls (TCGETA 0x5405, TCSETA 0x5406, TCSETAW 0x5407, TCSETAF 0x5408) wherever it accepts the corresponding modern `struct termios` ones (TCGETS/TCSETS/TCSETSW/TCSETSF), operating on the same underlying line-discipline state and differing only in the userspace representation: the four flag words narrowed to u16, c_line copied, and the first NCC=8 control characters copied. A consequence that is the real rule under test: an ioctl command that the device does in fact support must be validated against its argument, so a bad or NULL argument pointer yields EFAULT; ENOTTY is reserved for commands the device genuinely does not implement, and must never stand in for a fault the kernel failed to reach.
owning_layer: The shared TTY ioctl layer: `Tty::ioctl` in kernel/src/device/tty/mod.rs:225-338 together with the type definitions in kernel/src/device/tty/ioctl_defs.rs, i.e. above any individual TtyDriver and above the pty master/slave split. This is the closest Asterinas equivalent of Linux's `tty_mode_ioctl`, which is the single place all tty types get their termios/termio handling. The pty master's whitelist at kernel/src/device/pty/master.rs:158-162 must be extended in the same change so the new commands are forwarded to the slave, but the handling itself belongs in the shared Tty and not in PtyMaster: putting it in PtyMaster would fix the target test while leaving serial, hvc and vt still returning ENOTTY.
linux_reference: Linux enforces this in the tty core, not per driver: `tty_mode_ioctl` in drivers/tty/tty_ioctl.c carries `case TCGETA:` in the same switch as `case TCGETS:`, calling `copy_termios(real_tty, &kterm)` and then `kernel_termios_to_user_termio()` (vs `kernel_termios_to_user_termios_1()` for TCGETS), returning -EFAULT when that copy-out fails; TCSETA/TCSETAW/TCSETAF sit alongside TCSETS/TCSETSW/TCSETSF and go through `user_termio_to_kernel_termios()` + `set_termios()`. Crucially the internal state is a single `struct ktermios` -- the legacy/modern distinction exists only at the copy_to_user/copy_from_user boundary, which is the design Asterinas should mirror (translate at the boundary, keep CTermios2 internally) rather than introducing a second internal representation. `tty_mode_ioctl` also computes `real_tty = tty->link` when the tty is a pty master, which is the same redirection Asterinas already implements by forwarding to `self.slave.ioctl`. Unknown commands fall through `tty_ioctl` to -ENOTTY, matching Asterinas's default arms. Verified empirically rather than from the source text (elixir.bootlin.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, git.kernel.org and man7.org are all unreachable from this container): the host probe above shows TCGETA/TCSETA/TCSETAW/TCSETAF all returning 0 on the pty master, ENOTTY only on a regular file, and the returned termio being an exact truncation of the termios, which is the observable signature of that shared-ktermios design.
other_callers: Every TTY in Asterinas, not just the pty. Four TtyDriver implementations instantiate the generic `Tty<D>` and therefore share the one `Tty::ioctl`: PtyDriver (kernel/src/device/pty/driver.rs:114, `pub type PtySlave = Tty<PtyDriver>` at :39), SerialDriver (kernel/src/device/tty/serial.rs:86, /dev/ttyS0 and the console), HvcDriver (kernel/src/device/tty/hvc.rs:79, /dev/hvc0) and VtDriver (kernel/src/device/tty/vt/). All four return ENOTTY for TCGETA today, so any program using the legacy termio interface -- notably older stty/getty-style code and anything built against SysV-era headers -- fails on the console exactly as it does on a pty. Within the pty itself both fds are affected: the slave hits `Tty::ioctl` directly and the master reaches it only through the whitelist at master.rs:158-162. Beyond the tty tree the defect is not reachable: TCGETA on a regular file correctly gives ENOTTY via `InodeHandle::ioctl` (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:344-354) falling to the `PerOpenFileOps::ioctl` default (:568-570), and that must keep returning ENOTTY after the fix -- ioctl01 tcases[5] and tcases[6] assert it.
suggested_direction: Three edits, all at the layer named above. (1) In kernel/src/device/tty/termio.rs add `#[repr(C)] #[derive(Clone, Copy, Pod)] pub struct CTermio` with `c_iflag/c_oflag/c_cflag/c_lflag: u16`, `c_line: u8`, `c_cc: [u8; 8]` -- must be 18 bytes to match the host measurement, so let the natural repr(C) tail padding stand rather than packing it -- plus `From<&CTermios2> for CTermio` (narrow each flag word with `as u16` / `bits() as u16`, copy c_line, copy the first 8 of the 19 c_cc entries) and the reverse conversion for the setters, which should start from the current termios and overwrite only the low 16 bits of each flag word and the first 8 control chars so the upper flag bits and c_cc[8..19] are preserved, as Linux's user_termio_to_kernel_termios does. (2) In kernel/src/device/tty/ioctl_defs.rs add, next to lines 8-11, `pub type GetTermio = ioc!(TCGETA, 0x5405, OutData<CTermio>);` and `SetTermio`/`SetTermioWait`/`SetTermioFlush` as `ioc!(TCSETA, 0x5406, InData<CTermio>)` etc.; the legacy `ioc!` form is correct here since 0x5405 has zero size and direction bits. (3) In `Tty::ioctl` (kernel/src/device/tty/mod.rs:230-335) add four arms mirroring the existing GetTermios/SetTermios/SetTermiosWait/SetTermiosFlush arms -- `cmd @ GetTermio => { let ldisc = self.ldisc.lock(); cmd.write(&CTermio::from(ldisc.termios()))?; }` and the setters going through `self.driver().on_termios_change(...)` + `ldisc.set_termios2(...)` and, for SetTermioFlush, `ldisc.drain_input()` + `self.pollee.invalidate()` exactly as the TCSETSF arm does. Finally add the four new aliases to the PtyMaster forwarding list at kernel/src/device/pty/master.rs:158-162. Do not add a TCSETAF-only special case and do not touch the default ENOTTY arms. Traps for verify: keep the regular-file path returning ENOTTY (tcases 5 and 6), keep cmd 9999999 returning ENOTTY (tcase 4), keep the fd -1 cases returning EBADF ahead of cmd decoding (tcases 0 and 1), and confirm the TCGETA arm actually faults on a bad pointer via `cmd.write` rather than validating the pointer early -- the two target assertions want EFAULT from the copy-out, and ioctl01 accepts a SIGSEGV death as an alternative pass so a run that segfaults the child is not evidence the errno is right.
